topic: Examining Single Session Peer-Teaching Instructional Approaches on Pre-Service Physical Education Teachers' Throwing Techniques

sources.title: Examining Single Session Peer-Teaching Instructional Approaches on Pre-Service Physical Education Teachers' Throwing Techniques
sources.authors: Beseler B, Plumb MS, Spittle M, Johnson NF, Harvey JT, Mesagno C.

findings.finding: Video analysis feedback during practice sessions leads to faster improvement in motor skill performance.
findings.quote: A single 20-minute session of peer teaching with video analysis feedback during practice led to rapid enhancements in non-dominant hand overarm throwing skills.

findings.finding: Peer-teaching interventions are effective for improving both technical performance and the ability to diagnose movement.
findings.quote: Participants in both the VAG and VG groups reported that their respective interventions improved their throwing and Qualitative Movement Diagnosis (QMD) skills.

principle: Using video analysis technology alongside peer-teaching can significantly accelerate the acquisition of new motor skills.
for_the_teacher: Provide a feature that allows learners to record themselves and review their movement immediately after a practice attempt.
Encourage learners to analyze their own movement or a partner's movement to improve their diagnostic skills.
